executive_delta: Runtime blueprint and provider-neutral contracts were delivered in session 1 and re-verified in every session since. This packet exists because AC-05 requires one and none had ever been emitted: the artifacts were published but never reported through the mechanism the ledger consumes, which is why BACKLOG.json still shows this task as READY rather than REVIEW. Re-verifying the artifacts against the UJ-RUN-001 handoff gate surfaced a defect in one of them: the tool-cycle detector joined its k-gram key on a NUL byte, the same non-injective encoding that error E6 had already fixed in the adjacent file. It is corrected, the encoding is now single-sourced, and two regression tests were added — the first one proved to fail against the old code before being accepted. Accepted weight is unchanged at 0/13.

facts.claim: The contracts package typechecks under strict mode plus six additional flags with exit code 0.
The runtime invariant suite passes 36 of 36 tests and the full contract suite passes 140 of 140.

The textual loop detector is evadable by changing a single token: Jaccard similarity measured at 0.7778 on a nine-token mission and 0.9130 on a twenty-three-token mission, both under the 0.95 threshold.
The original idempotency key construction was ambiguous: two different field splits hashed to the same key. Corrected with length-prefixed encoding and pinned by a regression test.
L5 Broad Autonomy is not representable in the type system, so it cannot be reached through a configuration mistake.

The tool-cycle detector built its k-gram key by joining the window on a NUL byte, which is error E6 in a second file. Measured: the sequence ["a","b\u0000c","x","a\u0000b","c","x"] reported a cycle that does not exist, because windows 0 and 3 encode identically. The NUL also made depth-guard.ts binary to git and grep, so the file was excluded from every text audit of the repository for four sessions.
The regression test for that defect was proved to fail against the previous implementation before being accepted: expected false, actual true. A check that cannot fail is not a check.
